page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9354P processor operating at 3.25 GHz. It features 32 physical cores and 64 vCPUs with a shared CPU allocation. The system is equipped with 768.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 960 GB SSD, and there are no dedicated GPUs. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several areas. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng ranks in the top 10% with a score of 3179.99, while multi-core performance is in the top 25% at 101731.42. Memory subsystem capabilities are notable, with uncached read-only large block bandwidth reaching 351.41 GB/sec (top 10%) and a PassMark memory score in the top 10%. Database operations perform in the top 10% with 32,639.26 operations, and Redis SET operations reach 91.34 million operations per second. Large language model inference speeds for a medium 7B model achieve 55.29 tokens per second for text generation, placing it in the top 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density, combining a large DDR5 memory footprint with 64 vCPUs on a bare-metal architecture. This profile is suitable for memory-intensive workloads, database hosting, large-scale Redis deployments, and CPU-based LLM inference tasks.
